companion.npm_status: not yet on npm: publishing aqua-companion is owner gate GB2. Until then install from the tarball above.

mcp_server.status: aqua-mcp-server 2.0.0 is built on the companion and is not yet published. Once OWNER publishes it (gate GB1), `npx -y aqua-mcp-server` runs it; until then use the companion tarball. Versions below 2.0 are legacy and must not be used.

hosted_mcp.transport: Streamable HTTP (POST JSON-RPC, JSON responses, stateless; no SSE stream)
hosted_mcp.scope: read-only public catalog tools, resources and prompts; no authentication, no workspace tools; rate-limited
hosted_mcp.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http aqua-public https://aquaidp.xyz/mcp

catalog_config.rule: publishable/anon key only; clients refuse any other role and fetch it only from https://aquaidp.xyz (or a local override file)

install.claude_code: claude mcp add aqua -- npx --yes https://aquaidp.xyz/companion/aqua-companion-0.2.0.tgz mcp --keychain
install.claude_code_with_workspace: claude mcp add aqua -- npx --yes https://aquaidp.xyz/companion/aqua-companion-0.2.0.tgz mcp --workspace <folder>/AQUA --keychain
install.npm_later: npx -y aqua-mcp-server   # once aqua-mcp-server 2.0.0 is published (GB1)

tiers.meaning: Always allowed. Only reads the workspace or the public catalog cache.
Stages private records in the user's local workspace (drafts, imports, evidence). Refused in --read-only mode. Never approves anything.
Acts only after the human confirms in the MCP client UI (elicitation). Without that capability it returns requires_human with the exact command for the user to run.
Never acts. Returns requires_human with the steps the user takes in the AQUA browser app (approve, sign, freeze/export, submit, attest).

intentionally_absent.name: run_migration
intentionally_absent.why: Database migrations change production permissions and require explicit owner authorization.

intentionally_absent.name: admin_platform
intentionally_absent.why: Platform administration (users, roles, billing, teams) is not a user capability.

intentionally_absent.name: configure_security
intentionally_absent.why: Security configuration (RLS, keys, service-role access) is owner-only and never handled by agents.

intentionally_absent.name: read_hosted_answers
intentionally_absent.why: Private answers live in the browser vault and this workspace; the agent never gets database or service-role access.

intentionally_absent.name: TRANSPORT=http (self-hosted HTTP)
intentionally_absent.why: 1.x served unauthenticated write-capable HTTP. 2.0 has stdio locally and the read-only hosted endpoint only.

journey.how: init_workspace (the user confirms the folder in the MCP client) or the user runs `aqua-companion init --path <folder>`; the passphrase is typed by the user, never sent through the model
the user puts past submitted applications in the workspace inbox/; import_history stages them; the user exports a backup and confirms them at https://aquaidp.xyz/history
import_local_application (a file in inbox/) or get_application_details for a catalog program
create_draft_version stages unapproved drafts; request_evidence / attach_evidence
the user runs export-backup, restores it at https://aquaidp.xyz/aqua-local and approves each answer on the browser review board
the user exports a browser backup into inbox/; sync_from_vault_export imports it; read_review_status shows approved with the hash preserved
prepare_packet (readiness), the user freezes/exports in the browser, verify_packet checks the export. Nothing is ever submitted by the agent.
